- Model consistently overestimates prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive (sentiment > 0.5) — apply downward bias correction by 2–5% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (sentiment < 0.3), model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to avoid missing downward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: model often peaks 1–2 days before true price action — adjust forecast to lag by 1–3 days for better alignment with actual price behavior.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d horizon: if model forecast is > 75% above recent 10d average, reduce forecast by 10–15% to reflect reversion bias.
- Sentiment-driven corrections: if sentiment is > 0.7, model should be 5–10% below true outcome; if sentiment < 0.3, model should be 5–10% above true outcome — use sentiment as a multiplier for adjustment.
- Overshoot after spikes: if model peaks > 10% above recent 10d high, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 5 days to avoid overcorrection.
